title: Report highlights need for stronger customs controls and cooperation to protect EU citizens and businesses
key_claim: Around 6 billion items were released for free circulation in the EU in 2025, three times the 2022 figure, e-commerce parcels are over 97% of shipments, and the EU control rate fell to 65 items per million imported with refusals below 10 per million.
frame_summary: Argues that customs enforcement of EU product rules is being outrun by e-commerce volume and that the fix is stronger controls, better cooperation between customs and market surveillance, and the incoming Customs Reform machinery, rather than fewer obligations at the border.
verbatim_quote: In 2025, around 6 billion items were released for free circulation, three times more than in 2022, largely driven by e-commerce from outside the EU. E-commerce parcels now account for over 97% of all shipments entering the EU, far beyond what customs and market surveillance authorities can handle through traditional methods.
verbatim_list: In 2025, the EU control rate fell to 65 items per million items imported. The rate of goods ultimately refused at the border due to non-compliance or because they posed serious risks, also fell to below 10 items per million.
In 2025, the best-performing Member State recorded a discovery rate 384 times higher than the worst-performing one.

Over 60% of checked toys, small electronics, cosmetics, personal protective equipment and food supplements bought online from outside the EU failed to meet EU product compliance and safety requirements.

Acting at the EU external borders, customs authorities are responsible for enforcing EU rules in a wide array of policy areas, the so-called Prohibitions and Restrictions (P&R), in addition to their traditional financial role of collecting duties and taxes.
notes: Annual product-compliance report under Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Carries the load-bearing detection statistics and the counter-case that underperforming Member States improved. title: Guidance and legal text on temporary flat fee on low-value imports which will apply until 1 July 2028
date_evidence:
Publication date
8 June 2026 (Last updated on: 20 July 2026)
key_claim: A temporary €3 customs duty per item applies to low-value consignments from 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028, and product identifiers become mandatory in customs declarations from 1 November 2026 to help authorities detect and block unsafe goods.
frame_summary: Argues that removing the de minimis relief is a fairness and traceability measure rather than a revenue or protectionist one, and presents mandatory product identifiers as the instrument that lets customs detect non-compliant goods it cannot physically inspect.
verbatim_quote: The €3 temporary customs duty is a flat fee, which will apply until 1 July 2028, after which normal customs duties will apply, depending on the type of good.
verbatim_list: In 2025 alone, almost 5.9 billion of such low-value items were directly shipped from third countries to consumers in the EU, without paying customs duties.
All goods in consignments up to €150 sold in distance sales (e.g. e-commerce to consumers), regardless of VAT scheme (IOSS, Special Arrangements, or standard VAT).

To enhance traceability, product identifiers (PIDs) will also become mandatory from 1 November 2026 (but can be declared on a voluntary basis already from 1 July 2026), helping customs authorities detect and block unsafe or non-compliant goods.

title: EU customs: Council and Parliament agree on landmark reform
date_evidence:
Council of the EU
- Press release
- 26 March 2026 20:30
key_claim: The Union Customs Code overhaul creates an EU Customs Data Hub and an EU Customs Authority, makes platforms and distance sellers the importer of record, and cites a fast-growing number of EU standards that must be checked at the border as a driver; the data hub reaches e-commerce on 1 July 2028 and all goods by 1 March 2034.
frame_summary: Argues that the customs union needs a modern toolbox because trade volume, e-commerce and the growing stock of EU standards checked at the border have outgrown national systems, and frames data centralisation plus reassigned importer liability as the remedy.
verbatim_quote: a fast-growing number of EU standards that must be checked at the border
verbatim_list: Under the terms of the agreement, the data hub will become operational for e-commerce goods on 1 July 2028. A phased rollout will bring all movements of goods into its scope by 1 March 2034.

The new rules also clarify that platforms and those selling into the EU by distance sale, e.g. via e-commerce, are considered the goods’ importer and responsible for ensuring that all customs formalities and payments are taken care of, rather than the final EU consumer.
In 2024, 2,140 customs offices, working 24 hours a day and 365 days a year, collected almost €27 billion as customs duties and handled the import, export and transit of more than 1,370 million items.

title: Droit de douane forfaitaire de 3 euros sur les ventes à distance de biens importés
key_claim: French customs sets out how the €3 flat duty is declared in DELTA H7 and DELTA IE, names the declarant cascade, and confirms the product identifier becomes a mandatory declaration data element on 1 November 2026 to guarantee traceability across the product lifecycle.
frame_summary: Argues, from the national administration's operational standpoint, that the change is primarily a declaration-data change rather than a tariff change, and that the new product identifier exists to make each parcel traceable through the customs system.
verbatim_quote: Ces mesures entreront en vigueur le 1er juillet 2026 et resteront applicables jusqu’au 1er juillet 2028, date à laquelle la réforme de l’Union douanière, intégrant le Datahub, sera pleinement opérationnelle.
verbatim_list: L’identifiant produit est une nouvelle donnée qui sera facultative jusqu’au 1er novembre 2026, et rendue obligatoire à cette date.

Les produits soumis à prohibitions et restrictions et les produits soumis accises (boissons alcoolisées, parfums et eaux de toilette) d’une valeur intrinsèque inférieure ou égale à 150 euros, exclus de H7, doivent être dédouanés dans DELTA IE et seront soumis au droit de douane forfaitaire.

frame_summary: Argues that the Digital Product Passport is becoming operational plumbing rather than a policy aspiration, and positions registered, machine-readable product data as the way compliance is demonstrated across the Single Market.

title: EU: Legislation and guidance on fixed €3 customs duty for e-commerce
key_claim: From 1 November 2026 customs declarations for distance sales should include at least the merchant and non-standardised manufacturer product identifiers, an obligation whose stated objective is better risk management and enforcement of prohibitions and restrictions.
frame_summary: Argues that the practical burden of the reform falls on declaration data and systems rather than on duty rates, and that marketplaces, postal operators and carriers should be reassessing whether they can even source the product identifiers they will be required to file.
verbatim_quote: The objective is to improve customs controls for e-commerce imports and support more effective risk management and enforcement of prohibitions and restrictions.
verbatim_list: From November 1, 2026, customs declarations for distance sales should include at least the M-PID and NS-PID.

This approach appears broadly aligned with the new concept of importer under the EU Customs Reform, which also moves responsibility closer to the party facilitating or organizing the import of the goods.
